title: Health Insurance in Berlin - Quick Summary
items: **46 statutory funds are open to a Berlin address**, not the 93 on the official register: 34 that are open nationwide plus 12 whose regional list includes Berlin. The rest are company funds you can only join through an employer.

**Only one number differs between them.** The general rate is fixed at **14.6 per cent** by law and the treatment catalogue is written into the Sozialgesetzbuch. The **Zusatzbeitrag** is the single figure each fund sets itself, and in 2026 it runs from **2.18 to 4.39 per cent**.

**Berlin’s own two funds are at the expensive end.** AOK Nordost charges **3.50 per cent** and is the 22nd cheapest of the 46. Innungskrankenkasse Brandenburg und Berlin charges **4.35 per cent** and is 45th. The ministry benchmark of 2.9 per cent is beaten by only seven of the 46.

**What the gap is worth.** Employed on 4,000 euro gross, moving from AOK Nordost to the cheapest open fund is about **317 euro a year**. A freelancer on the same figure keeps **634 euro**, because there is no employer half. A student keeps **135 euro**.

**Everything stops at 5,812.50 euro a month.** That is the 2026 assessment ceiling, so above it the difference between two funds freezes at about **64 euro a month**, or 771 a year, however much more you earn.

**Two dates decide whether you can move.** You are bound to a fund for **twelve months**, and a change takes effect at the **end of the second calendar month** after you declare it. You never cancel yourself: the new fund tells the old one, and there is no gap in cover.
